newsitem.title: GERMANY: DASA clarifies Eurofighter funding idea.
newsitem.headline: DASA clarifies Eurofighter funding idea.

text.p: The head of Germany's Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG (DASA) on Monday said his company could help finance the Eurofighter combat jet by repaying state pre-financing for its Airbus civilian jet operations early.

Chief executive Manfred Bischoff told the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung (FAZ) that early repayments on sales-related aid for Airbus could free up one billion marks for the four-country Eurofighter project.

But he dismissed reports that DASA would make available for early repayment a separate 10.5 billion marks in pre-financing which is due to be repaid out of profits from its Hamburg-based Airbus unit from 2001 onwards, Bischoff said.
"DASA does not want to pay money out of profits which are by no means certain," the FAZ quoted Bischoff as saying.

Bonn is trying to close a two billion mark funding gap to pay the 23 billion mark price cost of the 180 Eurofighters it wants to buy, but has delayed ordering because of its problems cutting borrowing to qualify for Europe's single currency.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel and Defence Minister Volker Ruehe have reached an informal agreement for half to come from the defence budget. Waigel last month floated the idea of recouping the remainder from the Airbus funding after strong orders boosted the planemaking consortium's profit potential.
DASA, a unit of auto maker Daimler-Benz AG, makes Airbus fuselages and is part of the grouping with British Aerospace Plc, Aerospatiale of France and Spain's CASA.
It is also teamed up with BAe and CASA in the Eurofighter consortium, alongside Alenia Spa of Italy.
Bischoff told the FAZ that DASA was prepared to make a contribution to funding the Eurofighter, because if the project failed "the whole military aircraft industry in Germany would be endangered".

A DASA spokesman, reached at the Paris airshow, confirmed that intensive talks were going ahead at expert level between DASA and Bonn government departments, but said no agreement had yet been reached.
